payload.description_as_reported: Limited-quantity promotions activate competitive anxiety and possessive desire due to scarcity of quantity, increasing perceived value; similar quantity-limit scarcity cues and stock-level counters are reported to boost social value identification, interactive control perception, and purchase intention across consumer psychology, persuasion, and live-streaming shopping literature.

domain_transfer.source_domain: consumer psychology, persuasion research, and live-streaming shopping

payload.pattern: Display a remaining-stock counter or badge on the product card or page when inventory falls below {stock_threshold} units to trigger competitive anxiety and increase perceived value.

provenance.title: An analysis of advance fee fraud on the internet
provenance.quote_or_locus: Interpretive findings suggest that advance fee fraudsters employ specific methods that exploit the bounded rationality and automatic behaviour of victims. Methods include assertion of authority and expert power, mimicking and referencing persons/organisations, providing partial proof/legitimacy, reasoning, reciprocation, creating urgency, and implying scarcity

provenance.title: Applying persuasive messages to reduce public outdoor smoking: A pseudo‐randomized controlled trial
provenance.quote_or_locus: Relative to a baseline and a control condition, interventions based on the principles of reciprocity, scarcity, and authority were most effective in reducing the number of observed smokers in front of the building entrance (41.5%, 45.7%, and 52.1% reduction rates, respectively
